# Prepare Gene Sets for Functional Enrichment

This script builds the gene set collections (KEGG pathways and GO Biological Process)
used by `03_gene_functional_saureus.Rmd`. It is run **once per strain** and caches the
result to `data/databases/`, so the enrichment script loads instantly and needs no
internet connection.

Three collections are built, all keyed on the **locus tags produced by the nf-core/rnaseq
pipeline** (`SA_RS...` for USA-100 / N315, `SAUSA300_RS...` for USA-500 / USA-300):

- **KEGG pathways** — retrieved from the KEGG REST API with `KEGGREST`. KEGG stores
  *S. aureus* genes under the older locus tags (`SA0001`, `SAUSA300_0001`), so we remap
  them to the current `_RS` tags using the reference genome annotation.
- **GO Biological Process (BP)** — the processes a gene takes part in. Read directly from
  the reference GTF (`go_process`), which already carries GO terms on each gene.
- **GO Molecular Function (MF)** — the biochemical activities a gene product carries out
  (e.g. binding, catalytic activities). Also read from the GTF (`go_function`). MF is
  better annotated than BP for this genome and roughly doubles GO coverage, which is useful
  given how few *S. aureus* genes carry a curated pathway assignment.

:::boxy
**Why read GO from the GTF rather than NCBI gene2go?**
The reference GTF already embeds GO terms on every coding gene, so the collections are built
entirely offline with no download. The alternative, NCBI `gene2go`, would need each gene's
numeric NCBI GeneID to join — but this genome's GTF annotates proteins by GenBank accession
(`WP_...`) and carries no GeneID, so that route is not available from the local files. The
GTF is the authoritative, self-contained source here.
:::

:::boxy
**Why a separate preparation step?**
Building the gene sets involves live KEGG API calls and parsing the genome annotation.
Doing this once and caching the result keeps the analysis script fast, reproducible, and
runnable offline. The two strains use different reference genomes and different KEGG
organism codes, so each is prepared separately — exactly the same per-strain
parameterisation used in the differential expression script.
:::

### Strain parameter

This script is parameterised by `strain`. Render it once per strain (see the render chunk
at the very bottom), or set the value here when running interactively.

```{r params-setup, echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
strain <- params$strain   # "usa100" or "usa500"
stopifnot(strain %in% c("usa100", "usa500"))
cat("Preparing gene sets for strain:", strain, "\n")
```

### Load Libraries

```{r libraries, echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(KEGGREST)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
```

## Strain configuration

Everything that differs between the two strains is defined in one place. The rest of the
script is strain-agnostic.

:::boxy
- **USA-100** was aligned to *S. aureus* N315 (`GCF_000009645.1`); KEGG organism code `sau`.
- **USA-500** was aligned to *S. aureus* USA300_FPR3757 (`GCF_000013465.1`); KEGG organism
  code `saa`.
:::

```{r strain-config, echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
git_root <- system("git rev-parse --show-toplevel", intern = TRUE)

strain_cfg <- list(
  usa100 = list(
    kegg_org = "sau",
    gtf      = "data/genome_files/GCF_000009645.1_ASM964v1_genomic.gtf.gz",
    rds      = "data/data-01-Staphylococcus_aureus/USA-100/salmon.merged.gene.SummarizedExperiment.rds",
    label    = "USA-100 / N315"
  ),
  usa500 = list(
    kegg_org = "saa",
    gtf      = "data/genome_files/GCF_000013465.1_ASM1346v1_genomic.gtf.gz",
    rds      = "data/data-01-Staphylococcus_aureus/USA-500/salmon.merged.gene.SummarizedExperiment.rds",
    label    = "USA-500 / USA-300"
  )
)

cfg <- strain_cfg[[strain]]
gtf_path <- file.path(git_root, cfg$gtf)
rds_path <- file.path(git_root, cfg$rds)

cat("Strain      :", cfg$label, "\n")
cat("KEGG org    :", cfg$kegg_org, "\n")
cat("GTF         :", cfg$gtf, "\n")
cat("Count rds   :", cfg$rds, "\n")

stopifnot(file.exists(gtf_path), file.exists(rds_path))
```

## Build the identifier map from the reference GTF

The reference GTF is the bridge between all three identifier systems. Each `gene` feature
carries `locus_tag` (the current `_RS` tag, matching the count matrix), `old_locus_tag`
(the older tag, matching KEGG), and `gene` (a human-readable symbol, where one exists).

:::boxy
Only about a third of *S. aureus* genes have a human-readable symbol; the rest are named
only by locus tag. We therefore key every gene set on the **locus tag**, which covers
100% of genes, and keep the symbol purely as a display label for the results tables.
:::

```{r id-map, echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
con   <- gzfile(gtf_path, "r")
gtf_l <- readLines(con)
close(con)
gtf_l <- gtf_l[!startsWith(gtf_l, "#")]

fields    <- str_split_fixed(gtf_l, "\t", 9)
gene_attr <- fields[fields[, 3] == "gene", 9]

grab <- function(x, key) str_match(x, paste0(key, ' "([^"]*)"'))[, 2]

id_map <- tibble(
  locus_tag     = grab(gene_attr, "locus_tag"),      # SA_RS... / SAUSA300_RS... (count matrix)
  old_locus_tag = grab(gene_attr, "old_locus_tag"),  # SA0001 / SAUSA300_0001    (KEGG)
  symbol        = grab(gene_attr, "gene")            # dnaA, ...  (display only)
) %>%
  filter(!is.na(locus_tag)) %>%
  distinct(locus_tag, .keep_all = TRUE)

# lookup: old KEGG tag -> current RS locus tag
old_to_rs <- setNames(id_map$locus_tag, id_map$old_locus_tag)

cat("Gene features in GTF        :", nrow(id_map), "\n")
cat("  with old_locus_tag (KEGG) :", sum(!is.na(id_map$old_locus_tag)), "\n")
cat("  with symbol (display)     :", sum(!is.na(id_map$symbol)), "\n")
```

### Cross-check against the count matrix

Every gene in the count matrix should be present in the map — this confirms the GTF and
the pipeline output are the same annotation.

```{r id-map-check, echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
se  <- readRDS(rds_path)
ids <- rownames(se)

matched <- sum(ids %in% id_map$locus_tag)
cat("Count-matrix genes          :", length(ids), "\n")
cat("Matched in GTF map          :", matched,
    sprintf("(%.1f%%)\n", 100 * matched / length(ids)))

if (matched < length(ids)) {
  warning("Some count-matrix genes are not in the GTF map — check the GTF/assembly match.")
}
```

## KEGG pathway gene sets

We fetch two pieces from KEGG: the pathway names, and the pathway-to-gene links. KEGG
returns genes under the **old** locus tags, which we remap to the current `_RS` tags. A
pathway is kept only if at least 5 of its genes map into this genome.

<div style="background:#fff3cd;border-left:4px solid #ffc107;padding:10px;margin:10px 0;">
  <strong>Tip:</strong> The first run queries the KEGG API (a few seconds). The result is
  cached, so later runs of the enrichment script never call KEGG.
</div>

```{r kegg-fetch, echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
org <- cfg$kegg_org

# pathway id -> pathway name
kegg_pathways <- keggList("pathway", org)
pathway_names <- str_remove(
  as.character(kegg_pathways),
  " - Staphylococcus aureus.*$"
)
names(pathway_names) <- str_remove(names(kegg_pathways), "^path:")

# pathway <-> gene links (gene names carry the "org:" prefix and old locus tags)
kegg_links <- keggLink("pathway", org)

cat("KEGG pathways found         :", length(kegg_pathways), "\n")
cat("KEGG gene-pathway links     :", length(kegg_links), "\n")
cat("Example gene id             :", sub(paste0("^", org, ":"), "", names(kegg_links)[1]), "\n")
```

```{r kegg-build, echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# split into pathway -> vector of old locus tags
kegg_by_path_old <- split(
  sub(paste0("^", org, ":"), "", names(kegg_links)),  # bare old locus tags
  str_remove(unname(kegg_links), "^path:")            # bare pathway ids
)

# remap old tags -> current RS locus tags, drop unmapped, require >= 5 genes
kegg_by_path_rs <- map(kegg_by_path_old, function(old_tags) {
  rs <- unname(old_to_rs[old_tags])
  rs[!is.na(rs)]
}) %>%
  keep(~ length(.x) >= 5)

# assemble the mulea-style GMT data frame (matches the E. coli script's structure)
kegg_gmt <- tibble(
  ontology_id    = names(kegg_by_path_rs),
  ontology_name  = pathway_names[names(kegg_by_path_rs)],
  list_of_values = kegg_by_path_rs
)
# fall back to the id if a name is missing
kegg_gmt$ontology_name <- ifelse(
  is.na(kegg_gmt$ontology_name),
  kegg_gmt$ontology_id,
  kegg_gmt$ontology_name
)

n_before <- length(kegg_by_path_old)
cat("KEGG pathways retained      :", nrow(kegg_gmt), "/", n_before, "\n")
cat("Genes covered by KEGG       :",
    length(unique(unlist(kegg_gmt$list_of_values))), "\n")
cat("Example pathway             :", kegg_gmt$ontology_name[1], "\n")
```

## GO gene sets (Biological Process and Molecular Function)

The reference GTF annotates each coding gene with GO terms on its `CDS` feature lines.
The human-readable `go_process` field holds **Biological Process** terms (what a gene is
*for*) and `go_function` holds **Molecular Function** terms (the biochemical *activity* of
the gene product). We build one collection from each. Cellular Component is omitted: it is
uninformative for a bacterium, which lacks the organelles that make location useful in
eukaryotes. As with KEGG, sets are keyed on RS locus tags and require at least 5 genes.

:::boxy
**How to read the two namespaces.**
BP names the process a gene participates in (e.g. cell wall organisation, stress response) —
the most direct read on a lifestyle contrast. MF names an isolated activity (e.g. ATP
binding, oxidoreductase activity) — more abstract, but better annotated in this genome and a
useful complement when a lifestyle switch is largely metabolic. Keeping them separate lets
you tell process-level from activity-level enrichment.
:::

```{r go-extract, echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
cds_attr  <- fields[fields[, 3] == "CDS", 9]
cds_locus <- grab(cds_attr, "locus_tag")

# Shared extractor: pull every "<field> "name|GOid|evidence"" entry for a namespace,
# returning one row per (gene, GO term). Both go_process and go_function share this format.
extract_go <- function(field_name) {
  raw <- str_extract_all(cds_attr, paste0(field_name, ' "[^"]*"'))
  tibble(locus_tag = cds_locus, go = raw) %>%
    filter(!is.na(locus_tag)) %>%
    unnest(go) %>%
    mutate(
      go      = str_remove_all(go, paste0('^', field_name, ' "|"$')),
      go_name = str_split_i(go, "\\|", 1),
      go_id   = str_split_i(go, "\\|", 2)
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(go_id), go_id != "") %>%
    mutate(go_id = paste0("GO:", str_remove(go_id, "^GO:"))) %>%
    distinct(locus_tag, go_id, go_name)
}

# Turn a long (gene, GO) table into a mulea-style GMT, keeping sets with >= 5 genes
build_go_gmt <- function(go_long) {
  sets <- go_long %>%
    group_by(go_id, go_name) %>%
    summarise(genes = list(unique(locus_tag)), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(map_int(genes, length) >= 5)
  tibble(
    ontology_id    = sets$go_id,
    ontology_name  = sets$go_name,
    list_of_values = sets$genes
  )
}

go_bp_long <- extract_go("go_process")
go_mf_long <- extract_go("go_function")

go_bp_gmt <- build_go_gmt(go_bp_long)
go_mf_gmt <- build_go_gmt(go_mf_long)

cat("GO:BP  annotations :", nrow(go_bp_long),
    "| genes:", length(unique(go_bp_long$locus_tag)),
    "| sets (>=5):", nrow(go_bp_gmt), "\n")
cat("GO:MF  annotations :", nrow(go_mf_long),
    "| genes:", length(unique(go_mf_long$locus_tag)),
    "| sets (>=5):", nrow(go_mf_gmt), "\n")
if (nrow(go_bp_gmt) > 0) cat("Example BP set     :", go_bp_gmt$ontology_name[1], "\n")
if (nrow(go_mf_gmt) > 0) cat("Example MF set     :", go_mf_gmt$ontology_name[1], "\n")
```

## Coverage summary

How much of the tested genome each collection annotates. Partial coverage is normal for a
bacterium — many genes are uncharacterised — and is itself worth discussing when
interpreting results.

```{r coverage, echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
kegg_genes  <- unique(unlist(kegg_gmt$list_of_values))
bp_genes    <- unique(unlist(go_bp_gmt$list_of_values))
mf_genes    <- unique(unlist(go_mf_gmt$list_of_values))
union_genes <- Reduce(union, list(kegg_genes, bp_genes, mf_genes))

coverage <- tibble(
  Collection = c("KEGG pathways", "GO:BP", "GO:MF", "All three (union)"),
  Sets       = c(nrow(kegg_gmt), nrow(go_bp_gmt), nrow(go_mf_gmt), NA),
  Genes      = c(length(kegg_genes), length(bp_genes),
                 length(mf_genes), length(union_genes)),
  Pct_of_matrix = round(100 * c(length(kegg_genes), length(bp_genes),
                                length(mf_genes), length(union_genes)) /
                          length(ids), 1)
)
print(coverage)
```

## Save cached gene sets

Both collections and the identifier map are cached per strain. The enrichment script reads
only these files.

```{r save, echo=TRUE, eval=TRUE, include=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
db_dir <- file.path(git_root, "data", "databases")
dir.create(db_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

kegg_out <- file.path(db_dir, sprintf("KEGG_Pathways_Saureus_%s.rds", strain))
bp_out   <- file.path(db_dir, sprintf("GO_BP_Saureus_%s.rds", strain))
mf_out   <- file.path(db_dir, sprintf("GO_MF_Saureus_%s.rds", strain))
map_out  <- file.path(db_dir, sprintf("locus_symbol_map_Saureus_%s.rds", strain))

saveRDS(kegg_gmt,  kegg_out)
saveRDS(go_bp_gmt, bp_out)
saveRDS(go_mf_gmt, mf_out)
saveRDS(id_map %>% select(locus_tag, symbol), map_out)

cat("Saved:\n")
cat("  KEGG GMT   ->", basename(kegg_out), "(", nrow(kegg_gmt),  "sets )\n")
cat("  GO:BP GMT  ->", basename(bp_out),   "(", nrow(go_bp_gmt), "sets )\n")
cat("  GO:MF GMT  ->", basename(mf_out),   "(", nrow(go_mf_gmt), "sets )\n")
cat("  ID map     ->", basename(map_out),  "(", nrow(id_map),    "genes )\n")
```

## Summary

| Item | Choice | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Gene set key | RS locus tag | 100% of genes covered; symbols exist for only ~1/3 of genes |
| KEGG source | `KEGGREST` (`keggLink`) + GTF remap | KEGG uses old locus tags; GTF bridges old -> RS |
| GO source | Reference GTF `go_process` / `go_function` (inline) | No download needed; GTF carries GO terms. NCBI gene2go unavailable (GTF has no GeneID) |
| GO namespaces | Biological Process + Molecular Function | BP = process (interpretable); MF nearly doubles coverage. CC uninformative in bacteria |
| Minimum set size | 5 genes | Avoids tiny, unstable sets prone to spurious enrichment |
| Symbols | Kept as display labels only | Readable where available, locus tag otherwise |
| Caching | One `.rds` per collection per strain | Fast, reproducible, offline enrichment script |

Run this once for each strain, then proceed to `03_gene_functional_saureus.Rmd`.
